title: Hamden search, rescue of 16 children, and arrests — June 30, 2026

data.name: Hamden child-welfare rescue and Siders family arrests
data.description: Law enforcement executing court-authorized search warrants in Hamden, Ohio, located 16 children in a residence and arrested four adult family members. Victim identities and the exact residential address are intentionally omitted.

temporal.precision: Ohio Attorney General reported search warrants executed at approximately 10 a.m. local time.

geospatial.notes: Exact residential address intentionally omitted because the location was the home of minor victims.

caveats: Adult arrests and the rescue are documented by the Ohio Attorney General; alleged underlying conduct remains subject to criminal adjudication.

title: Vinton County Siders child-endangerment and sexual-offense prosecution

data.case_name: Vinton County Siders child-endangerment and sexual-offense prosecution
data.court: Vinton County Court of Common Pleas
data.case_type: criminal — child endangering, sexual battery, and unlawful sexual conduct with a minor
claims: On August 21, 2026, Gary Siders Jr. was indicted on two counts of sexual battery (F3) and two counts of unlawful sexual conduct with a minor (F3).
On August 21, 2026, Elizabeth Siders was indicted on two counts of sexual battery (F3) and two counts of unlawful sexual conduct with a minor (F3).
On August 21, 2026, Gary Siders Jr., Elizabeth Siders, and Christina Siders were each indicted on 19 child-endangerment counts: two F2, 10 F3, and seven M1.
On August 21, 2026, Gary Siders Sr. was indicted on 16 child-endangerment counts: 10 F3 and six M1.

docket_entries.description: Ohio Attorney General reported that all four defendants were arraigned in Vinton County Court of Common Pleas and each faced 16 second-degree felony counts of endangering children.

The U.S. Sun reported that Vinton County Prosecutor William Archer opposed Elizabeth Siders' release motion and said a grand jury was considering additional serious felony charges against her. Details were not provided; this packet does not represent those potential charges as filed.

Ohio Attorney General-origin reporting states that a Vinton County grand jury indicted Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders on sexual-battery and unlawful-sexual-conduct charges and returned revised child-endangerment indictments against all four Siders adults. Some child-endangerment counts are charged in the alternative.

gaps: Specific public case numbers and the underlying charging instruments were not separately ingested in this pass.
caveats: Indictments and charges are allegations, not convictions.
The August 21 release states that some child-endangerment counts are charged in the alternative; raw count totals must not be treated as a count of distinct acts.
Protected-minor identities and re-identifying details are intentionally excluded. The sex-offense victim is represented only by the anonymous research label Minor Victim A when a handle is necessary.
The August 18 report about potential additional charges is retained as historical provenance but is superseded as the current procedural posture by the August 21 indictments.

title: Evidence: 16 children located and removed during Hamden search

data.claim: The Ohio Attorney General reported that investigators executing search warrants in Hamden located 16 children; the children were removed from the home, evaluated at hospitals, and placed in temporary state custody.
